title: Unified iterator API and backoff helpers for embeddings + rerank across Py/TS/Go
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers use embeddings and reranking APIs at scale. Each SDK currently exposes different pagination and streaming ergonomics and inconsistent retry/backoff behaviour which makes porting client logic error-prone and increases support surface. Goal: ship a small, idiomatic shim in Python/TypeScript/Go that provides a consistent iterator-based pagination helper, a batching helper that integrates with our token/batch sizing guidance, and a unified retry/backoff policy with streaming-friendly semantics. Deliverables: 1) Iterator helper that transparently paginates embeddings/rerank results with optional prefetch; 2) BatchBuilder utility to build request batches by token/embedding-unit budget; 3) Retry policy that is idempotency-aware (retries safe ops, streams use reconnect with resume token) and exposes hooks for customers to customize; 4) Example snippets + integration tests for Py/TS/Go; 5) Documentation + migration notes.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs expose a stable iterator API for embeddings.list and rerank.list with identical semantics
BatchBuilder respects max_tokens and max_items constraints and exposes a simple size_estimator hook
Retry policy defaults to exponential backoff with jitter, capped at 60s, and supports immediate fast-fail on client-cancel
Streaming responses recover using server-provided resume_token when available; SDKs surface a reconnect helper
End-to-end examples added to /examples and unit+integration tests cover pagination, batching, and retry paths
Performance parity: latency/regression tests show <5% overhead from helpers in common workloads
design_decisions: Iterator is pull-based: next() fetches pages lazily, with optional prefetch thread/goroutine in SDKs where idiomatic
BatchBuilder will accept a pluggable size_estimator to adapt to future model token heuristics; default uses simple token estimate per item
Retry policy distinguishes idempotent (embeddings retrieval, rerank queries) vs non-idempotent (mutating endpoints). Default retries enabled for idempotent only
Streaming reconnect will prefer resume_token provided by service. If resume_token absent, SDK will fallback to user-facing error and expose helper to retry from start
APIs will avoid altering existing method signatures; these are additional helper classes/functions exported from top-level SDK module
Backpressure: helpers do not buffer unboundedly; prefetch default is 1 page and configurable up to 4 pages
implementation_plan: Week 1: Define shared behaviors and small design doc + API surface sketches for Py/TS/Go. Get PM + DX signoff.
Week 2: Implement Python helpers (iterator, BatchBuilder, retry wrapper) + unit tests. Add examples in examples/py/.
Week 3: Implement TypeScript helpers with Promise/AsyncIterator ergonomics + tests + examples.
Week 4: Implement Go helpers with idiomatic channels/iterators and context-aware retries. Add integration tests.
Week 5: Cross-SDK QA, benchmarks, docs, and lightweight migration guide. Cut release branch and coordinated SDK minor releases.

example_snippets:
Python iterator example:

from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient()
iter = client.list_embeddings_iterator(query='finserv corpus', page_size=128, prefetch=1)
for page in iter:
    for emb in page.items:
        process(emb)
